tagline: Down the Wilderness Road from Cumberland Gap to the Smokies.
intro: From the Kentucky line at Cumberland Gap, US 25E comes south on the line of the old Wilderness Road and climbs Clinch Mountain, where it looks down across the Great Valley of Tennessee. The cut at the top was made in the 1980s, two hundred feet below the old gap. At the foot is Bean Station, which grew where the Wilderness Road crossed the Great Indian Warpath. Its 40-room tavern once put up Andrew Jackson, Andrew Johnson and James K. Polk.
From there the road runs on through Morristown and White Pine to Newport on the Pigeon River, then follows US 25 through Del Rio to the North Carolina line.

moments.title: Abraham Lincoln Library and Museum
moments.text: At Harrogate a university founded in Lincoln's honor took over the grounds of a failed 700-room hotel. Its museum keeps the cane Lincoln carried to Ford's Theatre.

moments.title: Bean Station
moments.text: In the 1940s the water behind Cherokee Dam covered the old town and its people were moved out. Bean Station started over at the new crossroads of 11W and 25E.

moments.title: Crockett Tavern Museum
moments.text: A log cabin built in the 1950s, at the height of the Crockett craze, stands in for the tavern Davy Crockett's father opened near here in 1794.
